sections.text: Every Rust program starts running at a function called main. Inside it, println! prints a line of text.
A function is a named block of instructions. The curly braces { } mark where it starts and ends. The computer runs the lines inside main from top to bottom.

Coming from another language: println! is a macro rather than a function because it needs to take any number of arguments and check its format string against them at compile time. Rust functions can't do either.

fn declares a function. println! ends with ! because it's a macro: a special kind of command that Rust expands into more code before the program runs. You'll meet more macros later. Most lines end with a semicolon (you'll see the exceptions later). Strings go in double quotes.

exercise.prompt: Change the program so it prints: Hello, Rust!
hints: Look at the text inside the quotes of println!. That text is what gets printed.
Change the word world to Rust. Keep the comma and the exclamation mark.

quiz.question: Where does a Rust program start running?
options: The first line of the file
quiz.explanation: Every Rust program starts running in the main function, wherever it sits in the file. Other functions only run when something calls them.

quiz.question: Why does println! end with an exclamation mark?
quiz.explanation: In Rust, a name ending in ! is a macro, not an ordinary function. println! is a macro that checks its format string while the program is compiled.
